newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends Tokyo unchanged, BOJ neutral.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends Tokyo unchanged, BOJ neutral.

text.p: The key March Euroyen futures contract on the TIFFE ended unchanged after fully recovering early losses incurred by corrective selling to Tuesday's rally, traders said on Wednesday.

The Bank of Japan (BOJ) has been conducting neutral money market operation since the new one month bank reporting period started on Tuesday. On Wednesday, it drained 600 billion yen from the market where it had projected 580 billion yen surplus.
Some traders said that there is a sign of a shift in capital flows from the shorter end to the longer end of the yen debt market.

Shoji Kitta, managing director of Japan's largest money broker Tokyo Tanshi Co Ltd, said: "Investors who had pooled funds in the money market and patiently waited for a rate hike have already started to move funds into the long-term debt market and into stocks as they gave up hopes of a credit tightening in the medium term."
Such pooled funds are estimated to total four to five trillion yen, Kitta said.
This movement, although not yet a major one, would affect short- and long-term yields in the Japanese debt market, he said.
The key overnight call rate was most actively traded at 0.47 percent unchanged from its weighted average on Tuesday.
The key three month certificates of deposits (CD) were traded at 0.53 percent. The CD rate has been unchanged since September 3. ---Yoshiko Mori, Tokyo Treasury Desk 813-3432-8676
